hint: The flat display on a phone or laptop that shows what you are doing.
sentence: You tap the _____ of your phone to open apps.
explanation: A screen is the display surface of a device.

hint: A powerful computer that delivers web pages and data to other computers.
sentence: When you open a website, a _____ sends the page to your browser.
explanation: A server provides data or services to client devices over a network.

hint: A number system that uses only two digits, the language of computer hardware.
sentence: Computers store all data as ones and zeros in _____ code.
explanation: Binary is base 2, which matches the on/off states of digital circuits.

hint: An endpoint that lets two programs exchange data over a network.
sentence: The chat app opened a network _____ to talk to the remote machine.
explanation: A socket is one end of a two-way communication link between programs.

hint: The core part of an operating system that manages hardware and memory.
sentence: Linux is built around a _____ that manages processes and hardware.
explanation: The kernel sits between applications and hardware and controls resources.

hint: An algorithm for turning readable text into a secret code.
sentence: A Caesar _____ shifts each letter by a fixed number of places.
explanation: A cipher is a method for encrypting and decrypting information.

hint: A large body that orbits a star, like Earth or Mars.
sentence: Earth is the only _____ we know that supports life.
explanation: A planet is a large body that orbits a star and has cleared its orbit.

hint: The ability to do work, which comes in forms like heat, light and motion.
sentence: Plants turn sunlight into chemical _____ they can store.
explanation: Photosynthesis converts light energy into stored chemical energy.

hint: A nerve cell that carries signals through the brain and body.
sentence: Each _____ passes electrical signals to the next one across a synapse.
explanation: Neurons are the cells that transmit nerve impulses.

hint: A positively charged particle found in the nucleus of an atom.
sentence: The number of _____ in an atom's nucleus decides which element it is.
explanation: An element's atomic number is its count of protons.

hint: A protein that speeds up chemical reactions in living things.
sentence: Amylase is an _____ in saliva that begins breaking down starch.
explanation: Enzymes are biological catalysts that lower the energy needed for reactions.

hint: A base that dissolves in water, with a pH above seven.
sentence: Sodium hydroxide is a strong _____ that turns litmus paper blue.
explanation: An alkali is a water-soluble base that neutralises acids.

hint: A trained professional who examines patients and prescribes treatment.
sentence: You visit a _____ when you need a medical check-up.
explanation: A doctor diagnoses and treats illness.

hint: The state of being free from illness and feeling well in body and mind.
sentence: Regular exercise and good sleep improve your overall _____.
explanation: Health is physical, mental and social well-being.

hint: A group of similar cells working together, like muscle or skin.
sentence: Muscle is a type of _____ made of cells that can contract.
explanation: Tissues are groups of similar cells that perform a shared function.

hint: A blood vessel that carries blood away from the heart.
sentence: Blood leaves the heart through a large _____ called the aorta.
explanation: Arteries carry oxygen-rich blood from the heart to the body.

hint: A life-threatening reaction to infection that can damage organs.
sentence: Doctors act fast on _____ because the body's response to infection can cause organ failure.
explanation: Sepsis is a medical emergency triggered by the body's extreme response to infection.

hint: A condition where the blood has too few healthy red cells to carry oxygen.
sentence: Low iron can lead to _____, leaving a person tired and pale.
explanation: Anemia reduces the oxygen-carrying capacity of the blood.

hint: The money a person or business earns over a period of time.
sentence: Her monthly _____ comes from her salary and freelance work.
explanation: Income is money received from work, investments or other sources.

hint: A plan for how you will spend and save your money.
sentence: Writing a monthly _____ helps you track where your money goes.
explanation: A budget compares planned income with planned spending.

hint: Borrowed money you promise to repay, or a record of how reliably you repay.
sentence: A good _____ score helps you get a lower interest rate on a loan.
explanation: Credit reflects your ability to borrow and repay money.

hint: Ownership value in a company or property after debts are subtracted.
sentence: Owning shares gives you a stake, called _____, in the company.
explanation: Equity is the ownership interest left after liabilities are deducted.

hint: A tax charged by a government on goods imported from other countries.
sentence: The government raised the _____ on imported steel to protect local producers.
explanation: A tariff makes imports more expensive to favour domestic goods.

hint: A neutral third party holds funds until a deal's conditions are met.
sentence: The buyer's deposit stayed in _____ until the home inspection was finished.
explanation: Escrow protects both sides by holding money until the agreed conditions are met.

hint: A large area covered with trees that shelters many animals.
sentence: Deer and owls make their homes in the _____.
explanation: A forest is a large ecosystem dominated by trees.

hint: Plants, animals and landscapes that exist without human creation.
sentence: Hiking is a great way to enjoy _____ and fresh air.
explanation: Nature is the physical world of living things and landscapes.

hint: The element in fossil fuels that forms a greenhouse gas when burned.
sentence: Burning coal releases _____ dioxide into the atmosphere.
explanation: Burning carbon-based fuels produces carbon dioxide, a major greenhouse gas.

hint: A cold, treeless biome with frozen ground beneath the surface.
sentence: Permafrost lies beneath the frozen _____ of the Arctic.
explanation: Tundra is a treeless region with a permanently frozen subsoil.

hint: Rainwater that flows over land instead of soaking in, carrying pollutants.
sentence: Fertilizer in farm _____ can pollute rivers and cause algae blooms.
explanation: Runoff carries chemicals and soil into waterways.

hint: A partnership between fungus and algae that grows on rocks and trees.
sentence: Scientists use _____ as an air-quality indicator because it is sensitive to pollution.
explanation: Lichens absorb pollutants directly, so their health reflects air quality.

hint: A vehicle that blasts off using powerful engines to reach space.
sentence: Astronauts ride a _____ to leave Earth's atmosphere.
explanation: A rocket produces thrust that lifts spacecraft beyond the atmosphere.

hint: A huge system of billions of stars, like the Milky Way.
sentence: Our solar system sits inside the Milky Way _____.
explanation: A galaxy is a vast collection of stars, gas and dust held together by gravity.

hint: The streak of light seen when a space rock burns up in the atmosphere.
sentence: A shooting star is really a _____ burning up as it enters the atmosphere.
explanation: A meteor is the glowing trail of a rock heated by air friction.

hint: A giant cloud of gas and dust where stars can be born.
sentence: New stars form inside a glowing _____ of gas and dust.
explanation: Nebulae are the birthplaces of stars.

hint: The point in the sky directly above an observer.
sentence: At noon on the equator during an equinox, the sun sits at the _____, straight overhead.
explanation: The zenith is the highest point in the sky, directly overhead.

hint: The point in an orbit farthest from Earth.
sentence: A satellite travels slowest at its _____, the far point of its orbit.
explanation: Apogee is the farthest point of an orbit; perigee is the closest.

hint: A structure built to carry a road or railway across a river or valley.
sentence: Engineers designed a long _____ to cross the river.
explanation: A bridge spans a gap so traffic can pass over an obstacle.

hint: A machine that converts fuel into motion to power a vehicle.
sentence: A car's _____ burns fuel to make it move.
explanation: An engine turns fuel energy into mechanical motion.

hint: A twisting force that makes something rotate.
sentence: A wrench applies _____ to tighten a bolt.
explanation: Torque is force applied at a distance from a rotation axis.

hint: A part that moves up and down inside an engine cylinder.
sentence: Burning fuel pushes the _____ down inside the cylinder.
explanation: Pistons convert pressure from combustion into linear motion.

hint: A large horizontal beam that supports the floors of a building or bridge.
sentence: A steel _____ carries the load of the floors across the frame of a skyscraper.
explanation: A girder is a main horizontal support beam in a structure.

hint: A slight upward curve in the middle of a beam or road surface.
sentence: Road builders add a slight _____ so rainwater drains off to the sides.
explanation: Camber is a gentle convex curve that helps shed water or counter loads.

hint: A place where children go to learn from teachers.
sentence: Kids carry their books to _____ every morning.
explanation: A school is an institution for teaching students.

hint: A period of teaching, or a piece of knowledge you learn.
sentence: The teacher explained a new math _____ to the class.
explanation: A lesson is a unit of teaching on a topic.

hint: An academic qualification awarded after completing a university course.
sentence: She earned a _____ in biology after four years of study.
explanation: A degree is a qualification granted by a college or university.

hint: The grounds and buildings of a university or college.
sentence: Students walk across the _____ between lectures and the library.
explanation: A campus is the land and buildings of a university.

hint: A long research paper written to earn a postgraduate degree.
sentence: He spent a year writing his master's _____ on renewable energy.
explanation: A thesis presents original research to earn an advanced degree.

hint: A scoring guide that lists the criteria used to grade an assignment.
sentence: Each row of the _____ lists a criterion and the points it is worth.
explanation: A rubric makes grading criteria and point values explicit.

hint: A large group of lands ruled by one emperor or government.
sentence: The Roman _____ once stretched across much of Europe.
explanation: An empire is a large territory under a single ruling authority.

hint: A medieval soldier who served a lord and fought on horseback in armor.
sentence: In medieval times, a _____ wore armor and rode a horse into battle.
explanation: Knights were mounted warriors who served a lord.

hint: A formal written agreement between countries.
sentence: The two nations signed a peace _____ to end the war.
explanation: A treaty is a formal agreement between states.

hint: An uprising by people against those who rule them.
sentence: Angry citizens started a _____ against the king's high taxes.
explanation: A revolt is a rebellion against authority.

hint: Describes the medieval system where lords gave land in return for loyalty and service.
sentence: Under the _____ system, peasants worked the land for a local lord.
explanation: Feudalism organised medieval society around land, loyalty and service.

hint: Someone who rules on behalf of a monarch who is too young or unable.
sentence: Because the prince was only a child, a _____ governed the kingdom for him.
explanation: A regent governs in place of a monarch who cannot rule.

hint: A building where historic or artistic objects are displayed for the public.
sentence: We saw ancient statues and paintings at the _____ on our school trip.
explanation: A museum collects and displays objects of cultural value.

hint: A person who performs songs with their voice.
sentence: The _____ stepped up to the microphone and began the song.
explanation: A singer performs music using their voice.

hint: A stretched cloth surface that artists paint on.
sentence: The artist stretched a blank _____ over a wooden frame before painting.
explanation: A canvas is the fabric surface used for oil and acrylic painting.

hint: A 14-line poem, famously written by Shakespeare.
sentence: Shakespeare wrote 154 of these 14-line poems, each called a _____.
explanation: A sonnet is a fourteen-line poem with a set rhyme scheme.

hint: A painting made on fresh wet plaster so the colors become part of the wall.
sentence: Michelangelo painted a famous _____ on the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel.
explanation: In a fresco, pigment is applied to wet plaster and dries into the wall.

hint: An artwork made by fitting together many small colored pieces of stone or glass.
sentence: Roman floors were often decorated with a _____ of tiny stone tiles.
explanation: A mosaic assembles small tiles or fragments into a picture or pattern.

hint: The set of three stumps and two bails that a bowler tries to hit.
sentence: The bowler cheered when the ball knocked the bails off the _____.
explanation: The wicket is the wooden target the bowler aims at and the batter defends.

hint: The player who delivers the ball to the batter.
sentence: The fast _____ ran in and delivered the ball at a hundred and forty kilometres an hour.
explanation: A bowler bowls the ball towards the batter's wicket.

hint: The official who makes decisions such as out or not out.
sentence: The _____ raised a finger to signal that the batter was out.
explanation: Umpires enforce the laws of cricket and give decisions on the field.

hint: The way a batter positions their feet and body before the ball is bowled.
sentence: The batter adjusted his _____ and waited for the bowler to run in.
explanation: A good stance keeps a batter balanced and ready to play a shot.

hint: A painted line on the pitch that marks where the batter must stand.
sentence: The batter stretched his bat over the _____ just before the throw hit the stumps.
explanation: The crease marks the batter's safe ground; a batter behind it cannot be run out.

hint: A deceptive delivery from a leg-spinner that turns the opposite way.
sentence: The leg-spinner disguised his _____, and the batter played for the wrong turn.
explanation: A googly looks like a leg-break but turns into the right-handed batter.

hint: A theatre where people go to watch films on a big screen.
sentence: We bought popcorn and tickets at the _____ on Saturday night.
explanation: A cinema shows films to an audience.

hint: A film genre full of chases, fights and explosions.
sentence: He loves any _____ movie with car chases and big explosions.
explanation: Action films focus on physical stunts and fast-paced sequences.

hint: The written text of a film or play, including dialogue and directions.
sentence: The actors rehearsed their lines from the _____ before filming began.
explanation: A script contains the dialogue and stage directions for a production.

hint: A company that makes films, or the building where they are shot.
sentence: The film was shot entirely inside a large _____ rather than on location.
explanation: A studio is a facility or company where films and shows are produced.

hint: A film that continues the story of an earlier one.
sentence: Because it continues the story of the original film, the second movie is called a _____.
explanation: A sequel follows on from the events of an earlier work.

hint: The last episode of a series, or the closing part of a show.
sentence: Millions of fans tuned in to watch the series _____ and find out who won.
explanation: A finale is the concluding episode or section of a performance or series.

hint: A team game where players kick a round ball into a goal.
sentence: Players may not touch the ball with their hands in _____ except the goalkeeper.
explanation: Soccer is played by two teams who try to score by kicking the ball into the goal.

hint: A racket sport played over a net on a court.
sentence: Players hit a yellow ball over the net with a racket in a game of _____.
explanation: Tennis is played with rackets and a ball on a divided court.

hint: A very fast run over a short distance.
sentence: The athlete won the hundred metre _____ in under ten seconds.
explanation: A sprint is a short race run at top speed.

hint: A barrier that runners jump over in a race.
sentence: The runner clipped the last _____ and stumbled before the finish line.
explanation: Hurdles are obstacles that athletes leap over during a race.

hint: A swimming event that combines all four strokes.
sentence: In the individual _____, swimmers race butterfly, backstroke, breaststroke and freestyle.
explanation: A medley requires a swimmer to use each of the four competitive strokes.

hint: A skiing race where competitors weave between poles.
sentence: The skier weaved between the gates in the giant _____ event.
explanation: Slalom is an alpine skiing race through a zigzag course of gates.

hint: A soft yellow spread made from churned cream.
sentence: She spread _____ on warm toast.
explanation: Butter is a dairy product made by churning cream.

hint: A food made from pressed milk curds, like cheddar or brie.
sentence: The pizza was topped with melted _____ and tomato sauce.
explanation: Cheese is made by curdling milk and pressing the curds.

hint: A strong-smelling bulb whose cloves are used to flavour food.
sentence: The chef crushed a clove of _____ into the hot oil.
explanation: Garlic is a pungent bulb made up of individual cloves.

hint: To cook gently just below boiling point.
sentence: Let the soup _____ on low heat for twenty minutes.
explanation: To simmer is to cook food in liquid just below boiling.

hint: To boil food briefly, then plunge it into cold water.
sentence: To keep their colour, _____ the green beans in boiling water for two minutes, then cool them in ice water.
explanation: Blanching briefly cooks vegetables and helps keep their colour.

hint: A Swiss dish of melted cheese eaten by dipping bread into it.
sentence: Guests dipped cubes of bread into the bubbling pot of _____.
explanation: Fondue is a communal dish of melted cheese or chocolate for dipping.

hint: A string instrument with a long neck, played by strumming.
sentence: He strummed a chord on his acoustic _____.
explanation: A guitar is a stringed instrument played by strumming or plucking.

hint: A small wooden string instrument played with a bow.
sentence: She tucked the _____ under her chin and drew the bow across the strings.
explanation: A violin is held under the chin and played with a bow.

hint: A sequence of notes that forms the tune of a song.
sentence: The singer hummed the _____ while the band worked out the words.
explanation: A melody is the main tune of a piece of music.

hint: The repeated section of a song that everyone sings along to.
sentence: The crowd sang along loudly every time the _____ came back.
explanation: The chorus is the part of a song that repeats, usually with the same words.

hint: The interval of eight notes between one pitch and the next of the same name.
sentence: The soprano's voice jumped up a full _____ on the final note.
explanation: An octave spans eight notes and doubles the frequency of the pitch.

hint: A classical piece for one or two instruments, usually in several movements.
sentence: The pianist performed a Beethoven _____ in three movements.
explanation: A sonata is a multi-movement work for a solo instrument or a small group.

hint: A piece of land completely surrounded by water.
sentence: You need a boat or a plane to reach a small _____ in the middle of the ocean.
explanation: An island is land surrounded by water on all sides.

hint: A very dry region with little rain and few plants.
sentence: Camels are well adapted to life in the hot, dry _____.
explanation: A desert receives very little rainfall.

hint: A low area of land between hills or mountains, often with a river.
sentence: The river flows through a green _____ between two mountain ranges.
explanation: A valley is a low stretch of land between higher ground.

hint: A deep, narrow gorge with steep sides, often carved by a river.
sentence: The river carved a deep _____ through the rock over millions of years.
explanation: A canyon forms as a river cuts down through rock over time.

hint: A narrow channel of water joining two larger seas.
sentence: Ships squeeze through the narrow _____ that links the two seas.
explanation: A strait is a narrow waterway connecting two larger bodies of water.

hint: A shallow body of water separated from the sea by a sandbar or coral reef.
sentence: Tourists swam in the calm _____ sheltered by a coral reef.
explanation: A lagoon is shallow water partly cut off from the open sea.

hint: A clever climbing animal with a long tail that lives in trees.
sentence: The _____ swung from branch to branch and grabbed a banana.
explanation: Monkeys are agile tree-dwelling primates.

hint: A small furry animal with long ears that hops and eats carrots.
sentence: The magician pulled a white _____ out of his hat.
explanation: Rabbits are small hopping mammals with long ears.

hint: A fast bird of prey used in the sport of hunting with trained birds.
sentence: The _____ dived at incredible speed to catch its prey in mid-air.
explanation: Falcons are fast birds of prey that hunt by diving.

hint: A reptile with a hard shell that it can retreat into.
sentence: The _____ pulled its head and legs into its shell when it felt threatened.
explanation: A turtle's shell protects it from predators.

hint: A large burrowing squirrel that lives in mountains and hibernates.
sentence: The _____ whistled a warning to the colony before diving into its burrow.
explanation: Marmots are ground squirrels that hibernate through winter.

hint: A fish-eating bird of prey that plunges feet-first into water.
sentence: The _____ hovered above the lake, then plunged feet-first to snatch a fish.
explanation: An osprey hunts fish by diving feet-first into the water.

hint: A count or amount, such as 7 or 42.
sentence: Seven is an odd _____ and so is nine.
explanation: A number expresses a quantity or count.

hint: A perfectly round shape where every point is the same distance from the center.
sentence: A wheel has the shape of a _____.
explanation: Every point on a circle is equally far from its center.

hint: The distance from the center of a circle to its edge.
sentence: If the diameter of a circle is 10, its _____ is 5.
explanation: The radius is half the diameter.

hint: A quantity that has both size and direction.
sentence: Velocity is a _____ because it has both magnitude and direction.
explanation: A vector has magnitude and direction, unlike a scalar.

hint: A rectangular grid of numbers arranged in rows and columns.
sentence: The determinant of a square _____ is a single number calculated from its entries.
explanation: A matrix is a rectangular array of numbers used in linear algebra.

hint: A quantity with size only, no direction, such as mass or temperature.
sentence: Temperature is a _____ because it has magnitude but no direction.
explanation: A scalar is described by a single number with no direction.
